name: Lavender (Floral)
lede: Lavender (Floral) is the brighter purple of the lavender bloom itself, kept apart from the muted, greyed [[lavender]] the web color lists settled on, and it carries the same hex code as our [[floral-lavender|Floral lavender]] article under a different name.

sections.title: Two names, one swatch
sections.body:
Lavender, the plant, gave English one of its oldest flower color words, but the muted, dusty purple most web color lists call "lavender" is greyer than the flower itself ever is [1]. Lavender (Floral) and [[floral-lavender|Floral lavender]] are the same computed color, #B57EDC, listed under two different display names in our library, with a color distance of 0.0 between them [1]. Our graph treats the two as the brighter, truer-to-the-bloom reading of lavender, next to [[light-hortense-violet|Light Hortense Violet]] at 3.6 units and [[orchid-purple|Orchid purple]] at 4.1 [1].

Wikipedia is the only source we hold for this exact name and hex pairing; no older dictionary, plate or survey in our library carries it [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive shows this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, within a color distance of 4, as photographed [2]. A bright, modern-saturation purple like this sits outside the range of the pigments and dyes historical painters had on hand, so its absence from the archive is expected, not a gap in our data [2].
